title: Reported job loss is followed by lower political action but not uniformly lower Congress approval in a CCES panel
source_unit: 9,500 respondents in the 2010–2012–2014 Cooperative Congressional Election Study panel; same-panel descriptive comparison using a 2012 retrospective job-loss item and 2014 political outcomes

observations.period: 2012 retrospective job-loss screen followed by 2014 political outcomes

denominator.unit: panel respondents with valid 2012 job-loss item and supplied panel weight; outcome-specific valid rows vary

job_loss_screen.unit: respondents reporting they lost a job during the prior two years in CC12_387_4

congress_approval_favorable.value: 13.86% after reported job loss versus 10.06% without reported job loss
congress_approval_favorable.unit: weighted share approving Congress somewhat or strongly in 2014; valid n=827 and 8,626

congress_approval_unfavorable.value: 80.85% after reported job loss versus 81.88% without reported job loss
congress_approval_unfavorable.unit: weighted share disapproving Congress somewhat or strongly in 2014; valid n=827 and 8,626

any_congress_contact.value: 37.36% after reported job loss versus 39.14% without reported job loss
any_congress_contact.unit: weighted share reporting any 2014 congressional contact route among visited/called/written/received/public-event/other fields

any_local_political_action.value: 23.93% after reported job loss versus 31.57% without reported job loss
any_local_political_action.unit: weighted share reporting any 2014 local political meeting, political sign, campaign work, or political donation

observations.method: Read the retained CCES panel Stata file; classify CC12_387_4=1 as reported job loss and =2 as no reported job loss; apply the supplied panel weight to 2014 outcome shares. Favorable Congress approval is codes 1–2 and unfavorable approval codes 3–4. Any congressional contact is any affirmative CC14_360x_2 through CC14_360x_8; any local political action is any affirmative CC14_417a_1 through CC14_417a_4.
observations.uncertainty: Job loss is a retrospective two-year item, not a dated separation, employer, reason, income loss, or benefit-loss event. The panel is selected and retained; the supplied weight's representativeness for this derived transition is not independently re-established here. Outcome-specific missingness, prior political identity, health, income, unemployment duration, local conditions, and other shocks remain. No replicate-weight or causal uncertainty estimate is claimed.
observations.subgroup: 2012 reported job loss versus no reported job loss among the retained three-wave panel; 2014 outcomes are separate valid-answer universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A job loss may reduce time, resources, or political action while leaving institution-specific approval shaped by party identity, attribution, economic expectations, or other conditions. The slightly higher favorable Congress share among the job-loss group is a counterexample to a uniform material-hardship-to-distrust rule.

related_sources.claim: The Cooperative Election Study identifies the 2010–2014 panel as a three-wave panel with 9,500 respondents re-interviewed in 2014.
The local audit records variable definitions, panel denominator, weighted calculations, and interpretation boundaries.

boundary: This is a same-panel descriptive follow-up from a retrospective job-loss screen to 2014 institutional approval and political action. It does not establish a dated job-loss effect, causal political response, trust change, attribution, remedy, household recovery, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Retained local 9,500-row CCES panel Stata extract; raw panel file remains outside the repository
